about: Juno's annotations, an invented case. Every participant turn in order, found by its opening words: its experiential statements, its exploratory note, its key quotes as said and the words highlighted. Then the times of the work and her PET board. make_demo.py builds the workbook from Juno's interview CSV, then her progress file and her themes file from this.

turns.at: Erm. That is a big question
es: Finding her already waiting on the second stair
Softening before the day has properly started
A house that is quiet and never empty
turns.en: Twice: just there. The stair is a boundary kept without being asked for. Quiet and empty come apart here, so presence is felt rather than seen.
kq: Even when it is quiet it is not empty.
turns.crux: Even when it is quiet it is not empty

turns.at: It is like being caught
es: Caught out by a tenderness never claimed before
Talking aloud to an animal at half six
Groaning back, and hearing it happen
turns.en: Caught, as if found out. Four years of no dog, then a whole conversation in a dressing gown. She laughs at the state of herself and keeps groaning back.
kq: I have started groaning back at her.

turns.at: My partner wore me down
es: Losing the argument to a photograph
Won over by the lean in the yard
Two versions of how the decision was made
turns.en: The photograph wins before the argument is over. Two stories of who decided, and she keeps both. The lean in the yard is the lean at the door now.
kq: once you have seen a photograph like that you have already lost the argument, you just have not admitted it yet

turns.at: Right. So the alarm goes
es: The day opening with who gets up
Cracking first, every morning
Not proud of being the one who goes
turns.en: Who gets up is the house's first question, and not always friendly. The whine outlasts them both. Cracking is her word, said against herself.
kq: I crack first. I am not proud of it.

turns.at: Annoying. No, it is more than annoying
es: Twelve minutes standing for something much larger
Anger taken off at the bottom of the stairs
Wanting to stay cross and not managing it
turns.en: She corrects her own word upwards. Twelve minutes stand for for ever. The wag takes the annoyance away, and losing it is its own annoyance.
kq: It is what the twelve minutes says.

turns.at: I would. Because then I could have it out
es: Never getting to have it out
Five years of the unsaid
A mood that does not survive the stairs
turns.en: A mood cannot be carried down those stairs. What goes unsaid between the two of them is counted in years.
kq: Five years of it never getting said.
turns.crux: She takes it off you at the bottom

turns.at: It is the same walk.
es: The same forty minutes, every inch known
Walked by the dog on some mornings
A hedge that has never once produced anything
turns.en: The route given in full, as if walked again in the telling. Five years of the empty gap, and still she has to check.
kq: there are mornings where I genuinely think she is walking me

turns.at: I love it. I did not expect
es: Surprised to hear herself say she loves it
Resenting forty minutes she did not have
The one part of the day that is hers
A respectable reason to be unavailable
turns.en: Resentment turned to love over the years, and it surprises her to say so. Out with the dog nobody can ask her for anything. Her head goes quiet by watching, not by thinking.
kq: And now it is the bit of the day that is mine.
turns.crux: it is the bit of the day that is mine

turns.at: Yes. It sounds ridiculous
es: Her enthusiasm for a wet hedge
No bad mood surviving that much joy
A child who will never be embarrassed by her
turns.en: Ten past seven, in February, every morning. The joy is the dog's and it reaches her. The child she compares her to never grows up and away.
kq: you cannot stand next to that much enthusiasm for a hedge and stay in a bad mood

turns.at: On the bottom field, yes.
es: Furious and thrilled while she runs
Aged four years at the gate
Letting her off every morning anyway
Her freedom worth the worry
turns.en: One of the best things she has seen, and furious the whole time: two at once again. She weighs it up every morning and always lets go.
kq: the look on her at full stretch is worth more to me than the twenty minutes of worry

turns.at: Erm. Yes. The first year was hard.
es: Her time stopping being hers
No more going off at an hour's notice
Six months in, thinking it a mistake
A thought never said to anybody
turns.en: Not the money but the freedom. A weekend away becomes a logistics operation. The mistake is thought, and kept silent.
kq: I have made a mistake here. I did not say that out loud to anybody.

turns.at: Because it is a terrible thing to say
es: Unable to regret a dog with a past
Her flinch at a raised arm, even now
Regret coming back on wet February nights
turns.en: Saying it would be terrible because of what the dog has been through. It went away, mostly. On a wet Sunday at ten it comes back.
kq: But I would be lying if I told you it never comes back.

turns.at: There was one. It was proper rain
es: Two minutes looking at the door
Her waiting, not begging
Turning round together at the postbox
Closer on the worst night than on the nice walks
turns.en: Stillness on both sides of the porch. That the dog waited without pushing is what got her. The turn at the postbox is made by neither of them.
kq: She was not begging. She was just waiting.
turns.crux: She was not begging. She was just waiting.

turns.at: I think because it cost me something.
es: Closeness proved by what it cost
Anybody can walk a dog in June
Giving up together as an agreement
turns.en: She hears herself sound grand and says it anyway. Cost as proof. Failing together turns into a bargain struck by the postbox.
kq: the easy days do not prove anything, do they

turns.at: Well, she has not signed anything.
es: Rules neither of them wrote down
Knowing where they stand without a word
A strange thing to have with another creature
turns.en: The joke first, then the list of the rules. An understanding with no conversation, which strikes her as strange once she stops to think.
kq: We have never once had a conversation and we both know exactly where we stand.

turns.at: Oh, it is the best bit of the day
es: Claws on the hall floor before the door opens
The lean, never the jump
The earless rabbit brought every time
turns.en: Coming home given in sound first, then in weight. The same lean as the yard five years ago. The rabbit muffles the whine.
kq: She puts her whole weight against your legs and stands there with her head down.

turns.at: It is being wanted. Plainly.
es: Being wanted, plainly
Nobody else that pleased to see her
Everything stopping when the key goes in
turns.en: Plainly, and with no bitterness, she insists. The hello from the other room is set beside it: fine, what adults do.
kq: I have never had a welcome like that off anything in my life.

turns.at: I think it makes me come home.
es: Once finding reasons to stay out
A clock on her now
Coming home for the door
turns.en: A stretch of staying out, said lightly, nothing dramatic. Now she wants the door bit. Her partner has noticed.
kq: But I want the door bit. So I come home.

turns.at: They said it once, in passing.
es: Back early for a Thursday
Hearing she will come home for the dog
Not pretending it is not true
turns.en: Said nicely and heard twice over. She does not know what to do with it, and will not deny it.
kq: you will come home for the dog

turns.at: Uncomfortable. But not in a way I could argue with
es: Uncomfortable, and unable to argue
The dog is easier
No memory of last Tuesday
What was going on still waiting in the hall
turns.en: The thought she keeps landing on and moving off. The dog needs nothing to have been got right. With a person the past is stood in the hall as well.
kq: She does not need me to have got anything right.

turns.at: Yes. Because I do not know what to do with it.
es: Forty stupid voices for her
Talking about her instead of talking
Unsure she wants to reach the bottom of it
turns.en: Two readings held open, good for us or a way round each other. Some weeks the one, some weeks the other.
kq: Or it means we have found something to talk about instead of talking.

turns.at: Yes. So in the spring she came up lame
es: Going straight to the worst thing
In the car inside four minutes
Doing the sums on the way
turns.en: A lurcher is all leg, so a back leg is not nothing. The sums she does on the way are about the end.
kq: it went straight to the worst thing

turns.at: My hands were shaking on the wheel
es: Shaking, when she is the one people ring
A bright calm voice she did not recognise
Her silence in the back as knowing
When did something come to matter this much
turns.en: Her competence gone, her voice a stranger's. The dog's silence read as knowing. Underneath, the question of when this happened.
kq: when did I let something matter this much

turns.at: Well. It was a thorn.
es: Fifteen minutes and forty quid
Crying saved up for the car park
Shocked at the size of what she felt
turns.en: Bathos, told against herself. The tears kept for the car. Not embarrassment, shock, she corrects.
kq: I saved that up for the car park

turns.at: It was out of proportion.
es: Organising her grief in advance, in traffic
A Saturday as a rehearsal
Finding the whole thing ready to go
turns.en: Grief already prepared. She is six, and lurchers are not a forty year proposition. The rehearsal tells her it is coming.
kq: So that Saturday was a rehearsal.
turns.crux: So that Saturday was a rehearsal.

turns.at: I try not to.
es: Trying not to think about the end
Watching her run in her dreams
Grieving a dog who is snoring at her
turns.en: Not much of an answer, she says. The running legs, and the thought she stops. She laughs herself out of it.
kq: it is a waste of a Tuesday evening to sit there grieving a dog who is snoring at you

turns.at: Oh, the groomer. Yes.
es: A foot taken away from the nail clippers
Two hours free at the groomer's
turns.en: Lighter, by request. The dog's disgust told with relish. Two hours set up as a gift.
kq: looks at me like I have suggested something disgusting

turns.at: Nothing. That is the honest answer.
es: Not knowing what to do with herself
A wrong quiet, like the fridge stopping
Looking at the second stair
turns.en: The free time does not arrive. The quiet is wrong, a noise only noticed once it stops. The stair again, empty now.
kq: it was a wrong quiet, like when the fridge stops humming

turns.at: Er. It was like the house was on standby.
es: The house on standby without her
A home arranged round her, never decided
A rule given up under a blanket
The house as a set, furniture waiting
turns.en: Standby, then a set: the house not lived in without her. Nothing was decided, it was arranged. The rule on the chair is going the way of the others.
kq: Furniture waiting for somebody.
turns.crux: It was like the house was on standby.

turns.at: Yes. And I did not like it at all.
es: Fetching her twenty minutes early
Floral and appalled
A whole house waiting for a dog
turns.en: She cannot wait the two hours out. Alarming, she says, only once it is said aloud to somebody.
kq: That a whole house can go on standby waiting for a dog.

turns.at: I suppose because of how much is resting on her.
es: So much resting on one animal
The thought she does not let herself finish
A dog who cannot be told any of it
turns.en: Two hours flat, and then what of longer. All of it on someone who cannot know she carries it.
kq: That is the thought I do not let myself finish.

turns.at: We do. Constantly.
es: Doing her voice, complaints about the service
The funniest thing in the house
Dog voices at half nine
turns.en: Laughter she defends as real, and then times. Half nine: when the voices come out.
kq: That is when the dog voices come out.

turns.at: Money. The fact that neither of us
es: A list nobody starts at half nine
Her mother unwell and not talked about
A dog as a door to close on it
turns.en: The list given in full, for once: money, next year, her mother. The chin on the knee as the legitimate way out.
kq: But the dog is a very good door to close on it.

turns.at: Two ways at once
es: Relieved, and uneasy about the relief
The reason they share a room at all
Not knowing which it is
turns.en: She names her own pattern, two ways at once. Separate floors before her, and now the sofa with a dog laid between them.
kq: So which is it. I do not know which it is.

turns.at: Good, because I cannot.
es: Round and round it without an answer
The answer changing with the week
turns.en: Glad not to be asked to settle it. The answer moves with the week she has had.
kq: the answer changes depending on the week I have had

turns.at: In the kitchen. That was the rule
es: Goodnight said out loud, as to a person
Two thumps of the tail, never three
Unable to skip the ridiculous ritual
turns.en: The rule held, more or less. The blanket was hers once. Two thumps counted exactly, and a ritual she could not skip.
kq: she just thumps her tail twice on the bed. Twice. Never three times.

turns.at: Erm. Probably the regret
es: The regret never said to her partner
Kinder to the dog than to the people at home
Patient with a sock, not with a cupboard door
turns.en: Two things unsaid, the first year and her unevenness. She knows it and does not know what to do about it.
kq: I know I am kinder to her than I am to the people in my house
turns.crux: I know I am kinder to her than I am to the people in my house

turns.at: Fine, actually.
es: Easier to say than she thought
Not a confession, just how it is
turns.en: She makes it ordinary: what most people with a dog would say with nobody they live with listening.
kq: It is not really a confession, is it, it is just how it is.

turns.at: Erm. Only that it is very ordinary.
es: None of it dramatic
Hair on the coat anyway
Into the middle of the house, on no particular day
Home with her in the description
turns.en: Her own summary, ordinary and wet. There was no day it happened. Home is described with the dog in it, without a thought first.
kq: if you asked me to describe home, she would be in the description and I would not have to think about it first

pets.title: Caught going soft, after four years of saying no dog

pets.note: Caught, as if found out. The photograph and the lean in the yard settle it before the argument ends, and the goodnight ritual is the tenderness she would once have laughed at. Home now has the dog in its description.
